title: Learning Science
description: How memory actually works — the rules this app is built on.

cards.back: The same study time works better spread out than crammed together
cards.note: It is why a card you review over weeks sticks better than one you drilled for an hour.

cards.back: Retrieving something from memory strengthens it more than re-reading it
cards.note: Also called retrieval practice. The effort of recall is the mechanism, not a measurement of it.

cards.front: Why does re-reading feel more effective than it is?
cards.back: Fluency is mistaken for knowledge — familiar text feels known
A study condition that slows learning down but improves long-term retention
cards.note: Spacing, interleaving and testing all make practice feel harder and the memory last longer.

cards.back: Mixing different problem types in one session instead of blocking them
cards.note: It hurts practice performance and helps the ability to choose the right approach later.

cards.front: What does Ebbinghaus's forgetting curve describe?
cards.back: Memory for new material drops steeply at first, then levels off
cards.hint: Named after the man who memorised nonsense syllables on himself

cards.back: You remember what you produced better than what you were shown
cards.note: Guessing before being told helps even when the guess is wrong.

cards.back: Explaining how and why something works, connecting it to what you know

cards.front: Roughly how many items can working memory juggle at once?
cards.note: The classic 'seven plus or minus two' is now thought to be closer to four without rehearsal.

cards.back: Grouping items into meaningful units so they occupy less working memory
cards.hint: How a chess master sees a board

cards.back: Pairing words with a visual representation so memory has two routes to it

cards.front: Why is a card that asks two things at once a bad card?
cards.back: It cannot be graded — you half-remember it and the schedule learns nothing
cards.note: One idea per card is the single most useful authoring rule.

cards.front: What is a leech, in spaced repetition?
cards.back: A card you keep failing, which usually means the card is badly written
cards.note: Rewrite it, split it, or pause it. Repetition will not fix an ambiguous question.

cards.back: Applying what you learned in one context to a different one
cards.hint: The whole point, and the hardest part

cards.front: Why does immediate feedback beat delayed feedback for beginners?
cards.back: It stops a wrong version of the answer being rehearsed
Continuing to practise after you have got it right
cards.note: Cheap in the short run, poor value compared with spacing the same minutes out.

cards.back: Recall is easier in the setting where the learning happened
cards.note: Varying where and how you study makes the memory less dependent on any one cue.

cards.front: What is the best predictor of long-term retention in a study session?
cards.back: How much you retrieved, not how long you sat there
